page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.4xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the average performance tier. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a single-core stress-ng score of 1876.98 and a multi-core score of 15440.75, supported by a 33 MB L3 cache. Memory bandwidth tests show 831.5 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 84.73 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In application-specific workloads, the server demonstrates a static web serving throughput of 16.69 GB/sec and handles 15.82 million Redis SET operations per second. For lightweight machine learning, it processes 135M model prompts at 1247.06 tokens per second, though performance drops to 32.03 tokens per second for 7B models.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is configured for compute-heavy tasks rather than memory-intensive applications. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing power without resource contention. However, the lack of bundled local storage means users must attach external block storage, which may introduce additional latency and configuration steps. The absence of a GPU also limits its utility for large-scale deep learning. Qualitatively, the hardware profile offers a balanced entry point for compute-focused workloads that require dedicated CPU cores without the premium cost of high-memory configurations.

This instance is suited for multi-threaded CPU tasks, software compilation, web serving, and moderate database operations. It is also appropriate for running lightweight inference models and general-purpose containerized applications.
